content: Dexlansoprazole is a medication that can cause several serious side effects, although these are less common. Below is a detailed explanation of these potential side effects and the actions you should take if they occur: 1. Kidney Problems: Dexlansoprazole may cause a condition called acute tubulointerstitial nephritis, which can occur at any time during treatment. If you notice a reduction in the amount of urine you produce or see blood in your urine, contact your doctor immediately. 2. Antibiotic-Associated Diarrhea: This medication can lead to an overgrowth of bacteria called Clostridioides difficile (C. diff) in the gut. Symptoms include watery diarrhea, persistent diarrhea, blood in the stool, severe stomach cramps, or fever that begins after starting or finishing the medication. If you experience any of these symptoms, contact your healthcare provider right away. 3. Severe Skin Reactions: Dexlansoprazole can cause life-threatening skin conditions such as Stevens-Johnson Syndrome (SJS) and Toxic Epidermal Necrolysis (TEN). Symptoms include painful red or purple skin that appears burned and peels, flat red rashes or blisters on the skin, mouth, nose, or genitals, and red, painful, watery eyes. If you develop a rash, stop taking the medication and contact your healthcare provider immediately. Seek emergency medical attention if you experience any of these symptoms. 4. Severe Allergic Reaction (DRESS): Dexlansoprazole can cause a rare allergic reaction called Drug Reaction with Eosinophilia and Systemic Symptoms (DRESS), which can affect multiple organs, including the liver, kidneys, and heart. Symptoms include skin rash or hives, fever, swollen lymph nodes, shortness of breath, swelling in the feet, ankles, or legs, dark-colored urine, or yellowing of the skin or eyes (jaundice). Stop taking the medication and seek immediate medical attention if you experience any of these symptoms. 5. Lupus: This medication may trigger or worsen lupus, an autoimmune condition where the immune system attacks the body’s own tissues. Symptoms include new or worsening joint pain or a rash on the arms or cheeks. Notify your healthcare provider if you experience these symptoms. 6. Vitamin B-12 Deficiency: Long-term use of dexlansoprazole (three years or more) can reduce the absorption of vitamin B-12, leading to deficiency. Symptoms include a sore tongue, weakness, or tingling and numbness in the hands or feet. If you experience these symptoms, stop taking the medication and contact your healthcare provider. 7. Low Magnesium Levels (Hypomagnesemia): Dexlansoprazole can cause a drop in magnesium levels, which may lead to serious complications such as seizures or heart rhythm problems. Those at higher risk include individuals taking the medication long-term or in combination with other drugs that lower magnesium. Symptoms include changes in heart rate or rhythm (e.g., fast or skipping heartbeat), dizziness, muscle spasms, or seizures. Stop taking the medication and contact your healthcare provider if you experience these symptoms. 8. Bone Loss and Fractures: Long-term use of dexlansoprazole, especially in older adults or at high doses, may increase the risk of bone loss and fractures. Discuss this risk with your healthcare provider if you are concerned. 9. Severe Allergic Reactions: Dexlansoprazole may cause serious allergic reactions. Symptoms include breathing difficulties, wheezing, a racing heart, fever, swollen lymph nodes, swelling of the face, lips, mouth, tongue, or throat, trouble swallowing, itching, skin rash, nausea, vomiting, dizziness, or fainting. Stop taking the medication and seek immediate medical attention if you experience any of these symptoms. Precautions: Allergies: Do not use dexlansoprazole if you are allergic to it, other proton pump inhibitors, or any of the ingredients in the product. Your pharmacist can provide a list of ingredients. Drug Interactions: Dexlansoprazole may interact with certain medications, such as methotrexate, digoxin, warfarin, tacrolimus, antiretroviral drugs (e.g., rilpivirine, nelfinavir, saquinavir), St. John’s Wort, and rifampin. Always inform your healthcare provider about all medications, supplements, and herbal products you are taking. Pregnancy and Breastfeeding: It is not known if dexlansoprazole affects pregnancy or passes into breast milk. Inform your healthcare provider if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding. Usage Instructions: Take dexlansoprazole only as prescribed by your healthcare provider. Do not share it with others, even if they have similar symptoms. Swallow the capsules whole. If you have difficulty swallowing, you may open the capsule and sprinkle its contents on one tablespoon of applesauce. Swallow the mixture immediately without chewing. Do not use dexlansoprazole for immediate relief of heartburn, as it may take 1 to 4 days to take full effect. Keep the medication out of reach of children. Missed Dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. If it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and take the next one as scheduled. Do not take double doses. Overdose: If you or someone else has taken too much dexlansoprazole, seek medical help immediately by calling 911 or contacting a Poison Control Center at 800-222-1222. Common Side Effects: The most common side effects include diarrhea, stomach pain, nausea, cold-like symptoms, vomiting, gas, headache (in children aged 12 to 17), and sore throat (in children aged 12 to 17). If these side effects bother you, inform your healthcare provider. If you suspect you are experiencing a side effect not listed here, contact your healthcare provider or report it to the FDA at 800-FDA-1088.
